text:
maria: quick question—after the offload RFC followup, do we want the allocator to expose a `migrate_on_evict` flag so the soft-evictor can do copy-on-access? i'm worried about fragmentation and the cost of full compaction.
ashok: +1 on the flag idea, but accounting matters. during migration we have two live copies for a brief window. peak VRAM could spike, which will affect Dedicated tenants.
joel: fwiw i ran a tiny microbench: on a few 1.2GB tensors, copy-on-access reduced tail latency but doubled peak usage. nums: p50 35ms -> 31ms, p95 120ms -> 105ms, peak_vram 1.0x -> 1.9x. ran on our p3-like canary nodes.
kevin: can we do chunked/streaming migration to avoid full double-allocation? copy in ~64MB slices with write-protect and retry on concurrent writes. keeps peak around +10-20% instead of 2x.
dana: streaming sounds good but it complicates residency bookkeeping and IO backpressure. also kernel memcpy choice affects perf a lot.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary deployed to pool 'evict-test-3' (3 hosts). Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/evict-test-3
maria: important: we must avoid ABI break. suggest an adapter layer that maps old alloc flags to `migrate_on_evict=false` defaults and feature-gates the new behavior behind a runtime flag.
ashok: adapter is fine. also add a per-tenant hard-cap guard: if migration would exceed tenant_quota, fall back to eager-drop (old behavior) and emit metric.
joel: another observation: fragmentation arises when we leave many small freed segments after streaming migration. suggest a transient "pin period" where newly-migrated segments are immune to compactor for X seconds to reduce thrash.
kevin: implement metrics we need: `peak_vram_ratio`, `migration_bytes`, `migration_time_ms`, `fragmentation_ratio`, `compaction_invocations`. surface in Console and alerts for >1.5x peak.
dana: i'll draft an RFC: "soft-evict adapter + streaming migration" — will include API sketch, adapter plan, canary rollout, metrics, and rollback plan. question: any constraints for Private (on-prem / KMS) re encrypted pages?
maria: yes — encrypted pages require KMS unwrap on host and cannot be streamed without touching keys. mark that as a hard constraint; streaming migration may be disabled for Private until we support remote unwrap.
joel: also add eval matrix: sequence-length distributions (short chat bursty vs long-context), tensor shapes, and KV cache hit-rate. eager demote + compaction helps short sequences, streaming helps long sequences.
kevin: perf nit: pick chunk size dynamically based on tensor size and current bandwidth. small chunks if network/PCI bus busy.
ashok: fallback semantics: if migration is taking >15s for an allocation, abort and revert to mark-for-evict (so compactor can reclaim) to avoid tail amplification.
dana: noted for RFC. i'll add a small sim harness to model fragmentation over a 24h tenant workload.
maria: can we also add a unit test for the adapter that verifies old flags preserve behaviour? i.e., `alloc(old_flags)` -> adapter -> no migration code path.
kevin: yes, add integration test: simulate concurrent writes during streaming migration and assert correctness + no data races.
joel: heads-up: remember KV cache semantics — if we copy a hot KV slab out-of-band we must update remote-index pointers atomically, otherwise we double-count residency.
maria: good catch. add an index-update hook that runs under allocator lock or via CAS in the KV layer.
ashok: ok let's sync tomorrow 10am to review RFC draft. if no objections by EOD, dana will flip the feature-gate in canary.
dana: will post RFC stub in #eng-runtime and link PR with tests. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks everyone.
